p: man with a measuring line in: This is the angel who was Christ: for in respect of his office he is often called an angel, but in respect of his eternal essence, is God, and so called.

Jerusalem shall be inhabited as towns: Signifying the spiritual Jerusalem and Church under Christ, which would be extended by the Gospel through all the world, and would need no material walls, nor trust in any worldly strength, but would be safely preserved and dwell in peace among all their enemies.
fire on every side: To defend my Church, to strike fear in the enemies, and to destroy them if they approach near.
be the glory in the midst: In me they will have their full felicity and glory.
forth: He calls to those who partly for fear, and partly for their own case, remained still in captivity, and so preferred their own personal benefits to the benefits of God promised in his Church.
winds of the heaven: As it was I that scattered you, so I have power to restore you.
Deliver thyself: By fleeing from Babylon, and coming to the Church.

glory hath he sent me to: Seeing that God had begun to show his grace among you by delivering you, he continues the same still toward you, and therefore sends me his angel and his Christ to defend you from your enemies, so that they will not hurt you, neither along the way nor at home.
apple of his eye: You are so dear to God, that he can no more allow your enemies to hurt you, than a man can endure to be thrust in the eye; Ps 17:8.
upon them: Upon the heathen your enemies.
they shall be a spoil to: They will be your servants, as you have been theirs.
sent me: This must necessarily be understood of Christ, who being God equal with his Father, was sent, as he was Mediator to dwell in his Church and to govern them.
